decisions.reason: The affine-intersection condition really is the earlier definition. The rejection also says no equivalence proof exists, but lem-diagonal-quasi-compact-iff-quasi-separated on the owning page proves it using affine product charts and finite distinguished-open covers. Corrected the convention and explicitly cited that existing proof; both definitions are equivalent.

The former sentence denies a valid implication: pulling the absolute diagonal back along X times_S X to X times_Z X gives the relative diagonal, because the two projections must coincide. Base change preserves closed immersions, so absolute separatedness implies separatedness for every structure morphism. The definition and base-specific converse remain unchanged.

The title incorrectly suggests that an affine target suffices, contradicted by the doubled-origin line over a field. The statement and proof correctly use affine morphisms: inverse images of affine opens are affine tensor-product spectra, and their diagonals are closed. Corrected only the title; the full three-part claim remains valid.

The old justification equates second projections before proving a=b. Invertibility of the diagonal and pr_1 Delta=id instead give pr_1=Delta inverse, hence Delta pr_1 h=h and b=a without circularity. The forward direction uses monicity to equate the projections and remains valid; an isomorphism is a closed immersion.

The target of each extension must be D, not Spec k: the two ring maps k[x] to k[t]_(t) yield lifts into the two charts and send the closed point to distinct origins. The overlap ring k[t,t^-1] is affine, but multiplication k[x] tensor k[y] misses t^-1, proving nonseparatedness. Also restored the universal pair quantifier in F2. F4 now quotes only the DVR definition; step 1.3 explicitly verifies the order-of-vanishing valuation and types the generic ring map through K.

The nonclosed-image hypothesis is necessary: the identity on Spec k has no boundary. The statement already includes it. The proof is sound: a finite affine cover yields one image whose closure contains t; localization away from its prime is nonzero and AC supplies a prime contracting inside that prime, giving the specialization. Corrected the title only.

F4 omitted the universal quantifier on affine pairs; one pair with U=W cannot imply separatedness. Restored that quantifier. The proof only needs its necessary direction to refute separatedness for the two V charts. DVR uniqueness is valid: if the generic image is generic then t survives and has positive valuation divisible by every n, an impossibility; closed generic images force unique residue-field maps.

Naturality in the target module M does not construct maps for changing A and B. Added the universal-property construction for a commutative square: d-prime composed with v is an A-derivation into the restricted B-module. Its unique linear factor gives the differential map; uniqueness proves identity and composition laws. The uniqueness proof of the universal pair remains valid.

F4 lacked the axiom that only zero has infinite value. Restored it: the explicit order-of-vanishing formula is finite for every nonzero rational function and sends zero to infinity. Its valuation ring is k[t]_(t); the two chart morphisms agree after inverting t and differ at the closed point, so the counterexample itself was already sound.

The integrality definition alone does not prove that V[x] is integral. The existing published integral-elements-subring corollary supplies exactly this claim for the nonzero subring V of K, so F9 and the dependency now license both lying-over applications. Checked maximal domination, the nonzero denominator clearing, and the monic equation for x inverse; explicitly handled the empty chain in Zorn.

An arbitrary A-linear map killing B need not be B-linear. F3 now requires the Leibniz rule, which gives D(bc)=bD(c) when D(b)=0. The actual quotient derivation in step 3.1 already satisfies Leibniz, so the inverse maps on differential generators prove the unchanged exact sequence.

B need not be a V^-1 A-algebra. The corrected proof constructs the base map V^-1 A to U^-1 B and precomposes its universal derivation with the A-algebra map B to U^-1 B. Also corrected the noninjective base map and the mistaken word multiplicative for the derivation. The square-zero-extension construction yields the fraction rule and mutually inverse maps.

The descended map B to Q is an A-derivation, not a B-derivation; for I=0 in a polynomial algebra it is visibly nonzero. Corrected its base ring and explicitly justified killing I times Omega using P-linearity. Leibniz makes the conormal map well-defined modulo I squared, and the two quotient maps are inverse on generators.

A local map V to a DVR can kill the maximal ideal, for example through the residue field k. The divisibility obstruction only applies when the generic image is the generic point and the field map K to Frac(A) makes t survive. Added exactly that hypothesis and explained the closed-generic-image case, where the fixed chart map is unique.

The sheafification definition supplies no objectwise module theorem. Constructed scalar multiplication and addition on germ-compatible plus presentations, then applied plus twice. Local representatives prove that the unique sheaf extension of a linear presheaf map stays linear. Tensor universality then gives the claimed adjunction and its cokernel preservation, with no finiteness or choice assumption.

The cokernel Q of I squared into I initially lives on Y. Defined the conormal term on X explicitly as i inverse Q, whose stalk at x is I_y/I_y squared and whose action factors through O_Y,y/I_y=O_X,x. The germ formulas now construct alpha on X. Affine quotient charts and exact localization give the same conormal sequence on every stalk, including the noninjective dual-number example.

The map from A to global sections of the inverse-image sheaf need not be injective, for example for the projection k times k to k. Replaced the inclusion by its canonical map. An S-derivation kills its image regardless of injectivity; localizing an A-derivation gives compatible maps on B_g and kills base fractions by Leibniz, preserving the comparison argument.

The proof uses separability twice: the primitive-element theorem supplies alpha, and separability of its minimal polynomial makes m-prime(alpha) nonzero. Corrected the explanatory sentence. Differentiating m(alpha)=0 gives d alpha=0, and every element of L is polynomial in alpha, so all generating differentials vanish.

The claimed congruence epsilon(a)b=ab modulo m squared is false for a=t,b=1. The exact Leibniz defect is the negative product (a-epsilon(a))(b-epsilon(b)), which lies in m squared. Corrected the sign and used this identity directly. The induced retraction sends da to [a] on m and splits the surjective conormal arrow, proving the stated isomorphism.

The localization requires the extra generator s inverse: B_s is presented by adjoining z with z sigma=1, not by the original variables alone. Corrected the presentation without changing finite type. Checked the remaining argument: rational maximal ideals have zero cotangent space, Nakayama makes their localizations fields, reduction and finitely many primes give C=K^r, and an inseparable element would inject a nonzero nilpotent into C.

Vanishing relative Omega gives uniqueness of square-zero lifts, hence formal unramifiedness, and cannot supply existence. Corrected the closing sentence to match the theorem and the opening paragraph. Frobenius still has zero map on absolute differentials but nonzero relative Omega, so it is neither formally unramified nor formally etale.
